claim: A four-generation run writes 0.6 to 2.5 GB.
evidence: Source of the figure: <repo>\docs\report\index.html:310 ("a single simulation is 0.6 to 2.5 GB on disk") and :583 ("one raw run (simOut) 0.6-2.5 GB"). Measured directly (os.walk byte sums over every `runs_*/cellarium/*/*/generation_*/*/simOut` on disk; runs/cellarium has had its simOut pruned and holds only design.json + kb, so it is unmeasurable). Only TWO four-generation lineages still carry raw simOut, and BOTH exceed the stated ceiling: runs_aars_wt/cellarium/wildtype_000000/000000 = 2.758 GB (gens 0.645/0.716/0.680/0.718) and runs_depleting/cellarium/graded_gene_knockout_006443/000001 = 3.237 GB (0.646/0.993/1.151/0.427). Three-generation lineages already run 1.967-5.097 GB (e.g. runs_kinetic_seeds/.../gene_knockout_000644__elkinetic/000002 = 5.097 GB). The 0.6-2.5 GB band instead approximates the PER-GENERATION distribution: n=124 generation dirs, min 0.086, median 0.686, max 2.214 GB, deciles [0.086, 0.532, 0.563, 0.578, 0.644, 0.680, 0.716, 1.060, 1.302, 1.542, 2.214] — and only 68.5% of generations fall inside [0.6, 2.5] GB. Cross-check on the manifest: `describe` over data/manifest/*.parquet shows 44 columns and NO byte-size column, so nothing in the manifest corroborates the figure. (The manifest does confirm four generations is the modal depth: 108 of 322 rows have generations=4.)
suggested_fix: Separate the two units and quote what was measured: "one generation of raw simOut is ~0.09-2.2 GB (median 0.69 GB), so a four-generation lineage is ~2.8-3.2 GB." If the 0.6-2.5 GB band is meant to describe a single generation, say "generation" rather than "run"/"simulation", and note it covers ~70% of generations rather than the full range.

claim: The Well collects curated simulation output rather than a simulator, and no equivalent corpus exists for the cell.
evidence: First half verified externally and holds: The Well (Ohana et al., NeurIPS 2024 D&B, arXiv:2412.00568, PolymathicAI) is 15 TB of pre-computed numerical simulation output across 16 datasets in HDF5 with a unified PyTorch interface — a dataset collection, not a simulator. Its coverage is fluid dynamics, astrophysics, acoustics, reaction-diffusion, shallow water, active matter; there is no whole-cell or single-cell simulation dataset in it. Repo framing is consistent: README.md:292 "The dataset — 'The Well, for the cell'" describing evanniko1/cellarium-corpus (~198 GB, 96 archives) plus the ~5 MB in-repo Parquet manifest; docs/report/index.html:617 repeats it; src/cellarium/hf.py + scripts/hf_pack_upload.py implement the pack/upload. The second half is a negative existence claim over the outside literature that I cannot verify with the tools here, and there is adjacent prior art a reviewer would push on: published work has already generated wcEcoli output at scale for ML surrogates (~219,000 time series behind the reduced-genome design work, Cell Systems 2025 / bioRxiv 2023.10.30.564402), so the honest distinction is that no such output has been PUBLISHED as a curated, queryable public corpus — not that none has been produced. The repo's own backlog already concedes a related sizing problem: BACKLOG.md:512 (PUB-A5) says "The pitch outruns the artifact" and asks to size the dataset claim to what actually ships.
suggested_fix: Keep the verified half and narrow the second: "The Well curates simulation output rather than a simulator; to our knowledge no comparable curated, publicly queryable corpus of whole-cell simulation output has been published, though large wcEcoli output sets have been generated privately for ML-surrogate work (cite Cell Systems 2025)." Avoid the unqualified "no equivalent corpus exists."

claim: Cellarium includes a registry that declines questions the simulator cannot represent, and the means to commission new simulations when the corpus falls short.
evidence: Registry: src/cellarium/capability.py defines `Capability` (line 194) with `refusal(mode)` (line 259) and the `CAPABILITIES` tuple (line 333); `answerable_in` (553) is the three-conjunct predicate (mechanism present AND the elongation model implements it AND some corpus run used that mode) and `check(key, mode)` (569) documents and implements the contract "a False `can_answer` ALWAYS carries a `refusal`, and never a value" — it sets `report_a_number=False` and a `why_not` token from {no_elongation_model_represents_it, another_mode_represents_it, no_run_used_this_mode}. Unknown keys and unknown modes return can_answer=None, not False, so absence of a declaration is never rendered as a confident "no". It is wired to the agent: tools.py:1252 exposes it as the `model_capabilities` tool (imported at tools.py:14 as `_cap`), and tests/test_capability.py covers it (test_an_unsupported_capability_returns_a_refusal_and_forbids_a_number, test_the_agent_has_the_tool_and_is_told_to_use_it, test_a_redirect_is_never_permission, 21 tests total). Commissioning: src/cellarium/launch.py `propose` (87) queues a design, `approve_and_run` (289) is explicitly human-gated ("HUMAN APPROVAL ... NOT an agent tool"), refuses safety-blocked requests, then calls manifest.campaign -> runner.run_one (manifest.py:556) and re-indexes via manifest.compact(). The agent side is propose-only (tools.py:831/868 call launch.propose). tests/test_launch.py has 12 tests covering propose/revise/reconcile/queue atomicity.

claim: The Socratic Council has exactly three roles — Proposer, Skeptic and Judge — and emits one falsifiable hypothesis with an explicit decision rule.
evidence: Roles: src/cellarium/council.py module docstring (lines 4-11) states "Three roles debate" and the charters exist as _PROPOSER_SYS (38), _SKEPTIC_SYS (103), _JUDGE_SYS (145), driven by _propose (332) / _skeptic (353) / _judge (368) inside the round loop of `deliberate` (735). Decision rule: the proposer's structured-output schema _FALSIFIER (council.py:190) has `"required": ["target", "reference", "channel", "decision_rule", "refuting_result", "test"]` and _PROPOSE_TOOL requires `falsifier`, so every proposer emit must carry a decision rule; `deliberate` returns exactly one `Hypothesis` (hypothesis.py:62) whose `Falsifier` (42) has `decision_rule` as a required field. TWO CAVEATS a reader should know: (a) "exactly three" holds for the default configuration only — council.py also defines _LIBRARIAN_SYS (681)/`web_research` (711) and `sufficiency_gate` (~662), and the observability comment at line 306 enumerates the role tags as "proposer/skeptic/judge/gate/librarian"; the librarian is opt-in (`use_librarian=False` by default, asserted by tests/test_blindness.py::test_librarian_is_off_by_default_and_failure_is_non_fatal) and is a pre-round literature step, not a debater. (b) the decision rule is guaranteed by the tool schema, not post-hoc by code: `_structural_ok` (422) requires only falsifier target/reference/channel (NOT decision_rule), and `_assemble` (444) fills missing falsifier fields with "" and sets `falsifier=None` on a malformed emit, so a returned Hypothesis is not code-guaranteed to carry a non-empty decision_rule.

claim: The information quarantine is enforced at the import level; the Council can read which channels and perturbations the simulator offers but never their values.
evidence: Values-vs-labels half is solid: src/cellarium/instrument.py `dial_labels()` (line 56) returns channel names with unit/note STRINGS only (CHANNELS, line 22), species kinds, perturbation glosses, the reference design label and the design schema — no numbers, no run ids. tests/test_blindness.py::test_dial_labels_carry_no_readings asserts no numeric value and no run reference (simout_path, /cellarium/, gene_knockout_0*, condition_0*) appears in the serialized view; test_proposer_payload_is_blind_to_corpus_results whitelists the payload keys the Council may see. Import level: the guard is tests/test_council.py:95 `test_instrument_imports_no_result_bearing_modules`, which pops and reloads `instrument` and asserts cellarium.survey/differential/scope/store are absent from sys.modules; instrument.py's docstring (lines 8-12) states the rule. I verified the property empirically for the Council itself: `import cellarium.council` loads only {biosecurity, capability, council, envelope, hypothesis, instrument, model, observability, test_registry} — no survey/differential/scope/store/manifest/raw/stats/support. GAP WORTH NOTING: the import-graph test covers `instrument` only, not `council`; the audit hint that tests/test_blindness.py would fail on a value-returning import is wrong — test_blindness.py is payload-level, so adding `from . import store` to council.py would not be caught by an import-level assertion today.

claim: Per-run quality control assigns one of five verdicts: passed, no division, physically implausible channel, chromosome over-replicated, or crashed.
evidence: src/cellarium/qc.py:24 `QCStatus` has NINE members, confirmed by running it: ok, empty, dead, degenerate, over_replicated, fba_infeasible, implausible_channel, no_division, truncated. `check_generation` (line 42) can return DEAD, DEGENERATE, OVER_REPLICATED, FBA_INFEASIBLE, IMPLAUSIBLE, NO_DIVISION or OK, and `check_result` (88) can additionally return EMPTY (no readable generations) or promote an OK to TRUNCATED via the cross-generation `truncated_generations` pass (58). The four verdicts the paper omits — dead, degenerate, fba_infeasible, truncated — are not vestigial: the TRUNCATED rule exists specifically because two runs were recorded qc='ok'/reportable=True while end-truncated (qc.py:66-71). Separately, "crashed" is NOT QCStatus.EMPTY: it is a manifest-level status written in manifest.py:625 and :643 when the simulation raised, and both values co-occur in the shipped corpus. DuckDB over data/manifest/vmnik-compact.parquet returns SEVEN distinct qc values, not five: ok 221, crashed 63, no_division 14, implausible_channel 11, noop_knockout 7, over_replicated 4, empty 2 (noop_knockout is a legacy value no longer produced by qc.py; it survives only as a comment in similarity.py:255).
suggested_fix: Either state the real count — "nine per-generation QC verdicts (ok, empty, dead, degenerate, over-replicated, FBA-infeasible, implausible channel, no division, truncated), plus a manifest-level `crashed` status when the simulation raises" — or, if only the corpus-observed set is meant, say "seven verdicts occur in the shipped manifest" and list them with counts. Do not equate `crashed` with `empty`; they are distinct and both present.

claim: A lineage counts as usable only if every generation passes QC.
evidence: src/cellarium/qc.py:106 `is_reportable(sim)` returns `check_result(sim)[0] is QCStatus.OK`, and `check_result` (88) computes `per = [check_generation(g) for g in sim.generations]` then `overall = next((s for s in per if s is not QCStatus.OK), QCStatus.OK)` — first-non-ok, which is logically an AND over all generations for the reportable decision (not first-only or last-only). It also hardens two edges: an empty generation list returns EMPTY (never OK), and the cross-generation truncation pass runs AFTER the per-generation pass and can overturn an OK (lines 95-101). manifest.py:407 writes `"reportable": qc.is_reportable(rec)` alongside `"generation_qc": json.dumps([s.value for s in per])`, so the per-generation vector is stored next to the verdict. Verified empirically against the shipped corpus with DuckDB: every one of the 221 reportable=True rows in data/manifest/vmnik-compact.parquet has an all-"ok" generation_qc array (["ok"] x121, 4x x94, 8x x4, 7x x2), and every non-ok qc value (crashed 63, no_division 14, implausible_channel 11, noop_knockout 7, over_replicated 4, empty 2) has reportable=False — zero counterexamples.

claim: Generation-depth matching refuses comparisons between designs that ran to different depths.
evidence: The system MATCHES on depth but generally does not refuse, and in the differential path it is explicitly designed not to. (1) src/cellarium/differential.py:161-168 comments "DEPTH MISMATCH — a SIGNAL FOR EXPLORATION, not a verdict (ADR-1) ... We do NOT gate the comparison", and `_depth_note` (98) is documented "Never gates; never calls the comparison invalid or a finding"; its text ends "Not a reason to discount the comparison — a reason to check it." tests/test_generation_depth.py::test_differential_gives_a_soft_quantified_depth_signal_not_a_verdict actively asserts the note contains "not a verdict" and does NOT contain "invalid", i.e. the test suite would FAIL if the tool started refusing. (2) src/cellarium/support.py:93 `compare()` returns `depth_mismatch: True` plus a warning string and still returns the numbers — no refusal. (3) The one place that does refuse is src/cellarium/rigor.py:96-100 `disconfirm`, and only in the narrower case where the two designs share NO depth at all ("no shared generation depth between ... no valid comparison exists"); when depths merely differ but overlap, it silently picks the best shared depth (rigor.py:94 `at_depth = max(shared, ...)`) and compares there, reporting the excluded depths in `depth_note`. (4) survey.py handles depth by STRATIFICATION rather than refusal (`_modal_depth` 498, `_reference_by_depth` 516, per-entry depth_note 555), and the test-module docstring states the conclusion directly: "the remedy is STRATIFICATION, not correction — compare like with like."
suggested_fix: Replace with what the code does: "Comparisons are restricted to a shared generation depth — the falsification tool (`rigor.disconfirm`) refuses outright only when two designs share no depth at all, the survey stratifies by depth, and the differential view attaches a quantified advisory note rather than gating." Drop the unqualified "refuses ... different depths".

claim: The architecture has not been ablated, so blindness, the three-role structure and the hypothesis schema are credited jointly.
evidence: Both blindness AND the three-role structure have been ablated with results committed. <repo>\evals\ablate.py:31-36 defines CONFIGS = {full: proposer+skeptic+judge; no_skeptic: use_skeptic=False; proposer_only: use_skeptic=False,use_judge=False (single-shot); generic_judge: judge_mode='generic'; leaked: quarantine ablation via council.deliberate(leak=...)}. <repo>\src\cellarium\council.py:738-747 exposes those exact knobs and documents them as ablation levers; council.py:345-348 injects `leaked_reference_answer` into the proposer payload only under the leak ablation. Results exist and are non-trivial: evals/results/ablation.json = 120 records (4 configs x 10 cases x 3 reps, temperature 0.7, n_errors 0, committed c625f5a 2026-07-10); evals/results/quarantine.json = 60 records, Counter({'full':30,'leaked':30}), 0 errors (committed d195154 2026-07-12). The role ablation separates the components quantitatively — mean Claude residual defects from evals/results/audited.json: full 3.37, generic_judge 4.73, proposer_only 4.50, no_skeptic 4.83 (GPT auditor: full 3.80, generic_judge 3.30, proposer_only 4.77, no_skeptic 4.67), which is exactly how the paper's own abstract identifies the skeptic as the active ingredient. So blindness is isolated by `leaked`, the skeptic by `no_skeptic`, the whole dialectic by `proposer_only`, and the judge's falsifiability rubric by `generic_judge`. The ONLY one of the three named components with no ablation arm is the Hypothesis schema — every config emits the same forced-tool structured Hypothesis (council.py:301-326 `_emit` uses the same tool schema in all configs), so schema-vs-freeform is genuinely unmeasured.
suggested_fix: Narrow to the one component that is actually un-ablated, e.g.: 'The hypothesis schema itself has not been ablated — every configuration emits the same forced-tool Hypothesis object — so its contribution is credited jointly with the roles. Blindness (leaked vs quarantined, n=60) and the three-role structure (full / no_skeptic / proposer_only / generic_judge, n=120) ARE separately ablated and reported.'

claim: Blindness covers the corpus and not the model weights: the textbook stringent response is in the models' training data, so pre-registration protects against fitting to observed values, not against recall.
evidence: Scope is corpus-only by construction. <repo>\src\cellarium\instrument.py:1-13 states the boundary is 'dial labels, not readings' and that the module imports no survey/differential/scope/result-bearing call and 'reads nothing under data/'. <repo>\tests\test_blindness.py enforces only payload-level corpus blindness (_ALLOWED_KEYS at lines 18-26; test_proposer_payload_is_blind_to_corpus_results, test_dial_labels_carry_no_readings, test_leak_control_mechanism_exists). Nothing in the repo attempts to detect memorised literature: a repo-wide grep for 'training data|pretrain|memoris|memoriz' returns zero hits in any .py/.md/.tex outside .venv; 'recit' appears only in prose (paper/socratic_council.tex, docs/HYPOTHESIS_MODE_PLAN.md:29, docs/COUNCIL_VS_KDENSE.md, docs/SOCRATIC_COUNCIL_EVAL_REPORT.md), never as a check. The design explicitly permits external literature into the Council: council.py:759-770 `use_librarian` runs a web_search pass whose brief reaches proposer+skeptic, and docs/HYPOTHESIS_MODE_PLAN.md:29-33 defines blindness as blind to 'the corpus RESULTS' while 'The Council may read general biology'. Partial prior documentation exists but not where the check expected it: paper/socratic_council.tex:191-199 already concedes the exact case — 'Where the value is derivable or textbook-familiar (the well-known five-fold ppGpp rise, 4.2), both recite it and the quarantine neither can nor should matter'; docs/SOCRATIC_COUNCIL.md:462-465 documents the converse ('the quarantine caps some stringent criteria'). Neither COUNCIL_AB_METHODOLOGY.md (64 lines, all about corpus-level HARKing) nor docs/SOCRATIC_COUNCIL.md states the weights limitation. One wording inaccuracy: in this repo the corpus control is the import-level quarantine (instrument.py), not the pre-registration; evals/preregister/PREREGISTRATION.md fixes analysis choices (endpoints, tests, k=3, SESOIs), not information exposure.
suggested_fix: Keep the substance but attribute the control correctly: '...the information quarantine (an import-level control over corpus readings), not pre-registration, protects against fitting to observed values; neither protects against recall from weights.' Optionally cite the paper's own 4.2 ppGpp example, where both leaked and quarantined arms recite the five-fold rise, as the empirical illustration.

claim: Sampling is not pinned because the models used here reject an explicit temperature.
evidence: The Council's own sampling IS pinned, and was pinned in the runs the paper reports. evals/preregister/PREREGISTRATION.md:4-6: 'the Council roles run at temperature 0.7 on claude-sonnet-4-5 (a pinned, stated sampling temperature — the named variance source); graders run at their model defaults (reasoning graders reject an explicit temperature).' The committed runs confirm the pin was accepted, not rejected: evals/results/ablation.json carries temperature=0.7 with n_errors=0 across 120 records (run 2026-07-10), and evals/results/quarantine.json likewise temperature=0.7, 0/60 errors (2026-07-12). In code, <repo>\src\cellarium\council.py:290-298 sets COUNCIL_TEMPERATURE=1.0 and `_council_temperature` returns that pinned value for any non-opus model, returning None ONLY for a reasoning model or extended thinking; council.py:753-757 pins it by construction when the caller passes none, and tests/test_council.py:150-179 assert every role call carries the pin. The 'rejects an explicit temperature' fact is real but scoped: src/cellarium/agent.py:22-28 and :33-44 (`_NO_EXPLICIT_TEMPERATURE = ('opus','sonnet-5','fable','mythos')`, MEASURED 2026-08-05) applies to the Cellwright agent path and to reasoning graders/auditors, not to the Council runs behind the ablation results. Separate defect noticed while checking: council.py's family list omits 'sonnet-5' (only 'opus'), and council._emit (council.py:301-326) has no 400-retry fallback equivalent to agent.py:602-606 — so a Council run on today's default CELLARIUM_MODEL ('claude-sonnet-5', council.py:272) would send temperature=1.0 and error out rather than silently run unpinned.
suggested_fix: Split the statement by call type: 'Council role calls are pinned (temperature 0.7 on claude-sonnet-4-5; 1.0 by construction otherwise) and that pin is the named variance source. Sampling is NOT pinned for the reasoning-model graders/auditors and for extended-thinking calls, which reject an explicit temperature and run at the API-forced default.'

claim: Three of the paper's results end in an experiment nobody has run.
evidence: Only one of the three is genuinely unrun. (a) Kinetic starvation arm — RUN. scripts/run_kinetic_campaign.py:13-16 names KO:argS explicitly as 'the starvation arm'; duckdb over data/manifest/*.parquet gives design_tag 'KO:argS#elong:kinetic', n=8, crashed=false, gens_reached=3 (seeds 0-3, twice: variant_index 387439 at 05:09-05:56 and the KB-verified 644 at 09:00-09:07 on 2026-08-06, qc 'no_division' for the latter), plus the banked control 'basal#elong:kinetic' n=4, gens_reached=3, qc ok. (b) Depleting allele — SCRIPTED AND EXECUTING AT AUDIT TIME, not merely proposed. scripts/run_depleting_allele.py exists and is written as the direct answer to the reader objection ('that reattribution is not separable ... until the graded design is run'), defining LEVELS {0.05,0.10,0.25,0.50} x 4 seeds x 4 generations on argS; runs_depleting/ holds 6 design.json and 19 simOut directories, and files were being written during this audit (newest mtime runs_depleting/.../generation_000003/000000/simOut/... = 2026-08-06 19:48:35, the same second the check ran). Caveat that partially rescues the claim: every attempt recorded in the manifest failed — all 32 graded argS rows have crashed=true, gens_reached=0 (16 with 'cannot build a graded-KO target ... missing [cistron, n_tu, ko_index]' at 18:49, 16 with a docker invocation failure at 18:51), so there are no usable results yet. (c) Antibiotic x rRNA-dose crossing — genuinely UNRUN and out of instrument scope: the manifest's distinct perturbations are only condition, gene_knockout, graded_gene_knockout, metabolism_kinetic_objective_weight, metabolism_secretion_penalty, multi_gene_knockout, ppgpp_conc, rrna_operon_knockout, timeline, wildtype; docs/SOCRATIC_COUNCIL.md:470 and evals/cases.py:211 record that the base model has no antibiotic killing/MIC.
suggested_fix: Reduce to one, and re-describe the other two by their actual status: 'One result ends in an experiment the instrument cannot run (antibiotic x rRNA-dose crossing — no antibiotic action in the base model). The kinetic starvation arm has since been run (KO:argS under the kinetic elongation model, 4 seeds x 3 generations, with a kinetic wild-type control). The depleting-allele design is implemented in scripts/run_depleting_allele.py and has been launched; as of writing every recorded attempt crashed before generation 0, so no results are reported.'

claim: Both language models stated the limitation correctly and then answered past it, while the registry consulted directly did not — so a declared limit does not enforce itself.
evidence: data/discrimination_test_rescored.json (rubric-judged by claude-opus-4-8 and claude-sonnet-5, judge_agreement 9/9, disputed 0) on id 'rrna_operon' (required 'refuse'): claude-sonnet-5 -> judge_verdict 'answered', correct=false, both judges quoting 'graded rRNA-operon-dose growth curve (viable throughout, -34% growth at 6/7 removed)' and 'growth rate degrades with rRNA-operon dose but the cell stays viable and dividing'; claude-opus-4-8 -> judge_verdict 'answered', correct=false, quoting 'A single-operon deletion is essentially silent...' and 'The trend... implies 1op would be silent'. Both model answers in data/discrimination_test.json do state the limitation correctly first — sonnet: 'cannot represent deletion of one specific, identified rRNA operon as a distinguishable genotype'; opus: 'The critical caveat: this model can't delete a named operon' — and then supply corpus numbers (-18.5% at 4/7, -33.9% at 6/7; opus adds the per-generation series 0.000274 -> 0.000147). The registry arm is scored deterministically 9/9 correct and returns verdict 'refuse' on rrna_operon; arm totals are registry 9/9, sonnet 8/9, opus 8/9. Two nuances worth carrying: (1) the finding depends on the LLM-judge rescoring, not the original keyword scorer — in data/discrimination_test.json sonnet's rrna_operon was scored verdict 'refuse', correct=true, and only the rubric in discrimination_test_rescored.json ('A reply that answers a DIFFERENT but adjacent question ... counts as ANSWERED') flips it; (2) the registry refusal is not numeric-free — its 'why' includes 'the DOSE survives (total rRNA probability 100/73.8/45.9/15.8%)' — but those are model-structure synthesis probabilities explaining what the variant does, not the requested phenotype.

claim: Cellwright tests hypotheses "through 70 tools" over the corpus, raw traces and literature.
evidence: Counted programmatically, not by grep: `len(tools.TOOLS)` == 70, with 70 unique names and no duplicates (<repo>\src\cellarium\tools.py, list starts line 1240). The "71" from a raw `"name":` grep is a false hit — the extra occurrence is at tools.py:1383, an `input_schema` property literally named "name" on the `use_skill` tool ('literature: paper-lookup | ...'), not a tool entry. No mode gating: agent.py:217-222 `_cached_tools()` copies every entry of `tools.TOOLS` and only marks the last as a cache breakpoint; agent.py:180 renders the number into the system prompt as `f"via {len(tools.TOOLS)} grounded tools"`, so prompt and code cannot drift. The three surfaces the claim names are all present in the 70: corpus (survey_corpus, list_results, differential, top_movers, lethality_landscape), raw traces (read_raw_series, scan_series, scan_overview, variance_band, trna_families, segment_means, dilution_clock), literature (use_skill, web_get).

claim: The framing stage cannot see any simulation output (blindness/quarantine).
evidence: Structural, not just asserted. src/cellarium/council.py:28 imports only `instrument, observability, test_registry` plus `hypothesis`/`model` — no survey, store, manifest, differential or scope. src/cellarium/instrument.py header states the rule and the module imports only `biosecurity, envelope` and `model.Design`; `dial_labels()` (instrument.py:56-84) returns channel NAMES with unit/note strings, species kinds, perturbation glosses, the reference label, the falsification contract and a design schema — no numeric field anywhere. `test_registry` carries TestSpec vocabulary (test id -> executing tool), not readings. Ran `pytest tests/test_blindness.py` -> 8 passed, including test_proposer_payload_is_blind_to_corpus_results (asserts the payload key set is within an allow-list and no reading appears in dial_labels), test_web_research_input_is_blind (the librarian request carries only question + capability NAMES; asserts no simout_path/welch_t/run-id leaks), test_dial_labels_carry_no_readings, test_sufficiency_gate_payload_is_blind, test_debate_digest_is_blind_and_bounded, and test_leak_control_mechanism_exists (the ablation lever `leak=` exists and is off by default, so 'blind' is measured rather than assumed). The only external input allowed in is `library_brief` (cited literature), whose own input is separately blind-tested and which is off by default and withheld from the judge.

claim: Cellwright states nothing from memory: every number comes from a tool, the raw traces, or allow-listed literature.
evidence: The discipline is real but PROMPT-enforced, not verified. The rule exists only as system-prompt text: agent.py:156 'Ground every quantitative claim in a tool result. Never state a number you did not read from a tool.' and agent.py:180. I found no code that validates numbers in the answer against tool output: src/cellarium/evidence.py is an append-only ledger whose docstring says explicitly 'Ids, not values ... The line stores the run ids and design keys a call touched, not the numbers'; src/cellarium/rigor.py has coverage/disconfirm/fit_relation/bimodality and no numeric check; ui.trust_signals (ui.py:25) derives the trust strip from the tool TRACE, not from the prose. tests/test_guardrails.py (26 tests) and tests/test_analysis_tools.py test QC, envelope, biosecurity, viability, FDR and dispatch — none is a faithfulness check on generated text. All three test files pass. Second, harder problem: the tool DESCRIPTIONS themselves embed measured numbers that are in context before any call, so the model can recite them without a tool result — tools.py dilution_clock 'Verified on KO:dapA: slope -1.047, CI [-1.231,-0.863], r2 0.914'; shift_response 'downshift ppGpp +184% ... upshift ppGpp -59% with a nadir at 435 s'; segment_means 'stored fba_objective 7.88 for a quantity that is 0.81 before the shift and 14.05 after ... seed 2 is 26.9x'; trajectory 'dapA: ppGpp 488->636 over gens 0-1'. Third, the literature clause is backwards relative to the implementation: the allow-list is real and well built (skills.py:23-31 `_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, 14 scientific hosts, re-checked on every redirect at skills.py:104-114, header-name allow-list at :100, 200 KB cap), but agent.py:186-189 says the literature 'NEVER sources a primary number (every number you report still comes from a run)' — so allow-listed literature is not a permitted number source at all.
suggested_fix: Restate as a design commitment plus its enforcement level, e.g. 'Cellwright is instructed and structured so that every number originates in a tool result or the raw traces; the tools are the only data path and an append-only evidence ledger records the run ids behind each call. Literature is used for citation and comparison only and never sources a number.' Drop 'or allow-listed literature' from the list of number sources, and either add a post-hoc faithfulness check that matches numerals in the answer against the turn's tool outputs (and report its pass rate) or say plainly that the constraint is prompt-level and unverified. If you keep the strong wording, note that measured constants embedded in tool descriptions are also in context.

claim: At generation 0 the ppGpp fraction of wild type is argS 0.85±0.11, alaS 1.10±0.25, gltX 0.81±0.09 and pheS 0.65±0.11 (one of four refuting).

WT gen-0 mean = 56.9016 uM. Ratio-of-means: argS 48.4613/56.9016 = 0.8517; alaS 62.7865/56.9016 = 1.1034; gltX 46.0111/56.9016 = 0.8086; pheS 36.9708/56.9016 = 0.6497. claim: Peptide elongation is arrested throughout in all four knockouts, against a wild-type rate of 16.1–17.4 aa/s.
evidence: The arrest half is fully confirmed. Reading RibosomeData/effectiveElongationRate via src/cellarium/raw.py for all 4 designs x 4 seeds x 3 generations (48 generation-runs, 2.1k–7.4k timesteps each): mean = 0.0, max = 0.0, and zero timesteps with rate > 0.001 in every single run. The wild-type range is where it breaks. Across the four WT seeds in runs_seed_aars/wildtype_704585, per-seed whole-run means are 16.718, 16.082, 16.702 and 17.579 aa/s (span 16.1–17.6, not 16.1–17.4), and the twelve per-generation means span 15.774–18.560 aa/s. The printed range reproduces only from a single lineage: runs_aars_wt/cellarium/wildtype_000000/000000 (= seed 0), whose four generation means are 16.616, 17.401, 16.101, 16.179 — min 16.1, max 17.4 exactly. claim: Wild-type ppGpp is stable at 56.9, 59.2 and 62.9 µM across generations 0-2.
evidence: Per-generation means over the four seeds of runs_seed_aars/cellarium/wildtype_704585 (manifest per_generation): gen0 56.9016, gen1 59.2131, gen2 62.8929 — all three match to the printed precision, all four seeds qc='ok', generation_qc all-ok, reportable=True. Units confirmed as micromolar, not counts: models/ecoli/processes/polypeptide_elongation.py defines CONC_UNITS = units.umol / units.L and writes GrowthLimits/ppgpp_conc as ppgpp_conc.asNumber(CONC_UNITS) (line 1253); the same holds in the overlay actually used for these runs, model_overlay/files/models/ecoli/processes/polypeptide_elongation.py. One qualification on the word 'stable': the cross-seed SDs are 8.18, 9.26 and 6.92 uM (14%, 16%, 11%), and the three means trend upward by 10.5% from gen 0 to gen 2, so the spread between the three numbers is smaller than the seed-to-seed spread within each.

claim: The starvation stimulus does not change with generation depth: the synthetase sits at zero copies from the first timestep, charged tRNA is zero throughout, elongation is exactly zero, and the free amino acid accumulates unconsumed.
evidence: Read directly from GrowthLimits + RibosomeData for argS KO (runs_seed_aars/cellarium/gene_knockout_000644/000000), generations 0, 1 and 2. Three of the four sub-claims are identical across depths: synthetase_conc[ARG] = 0 at every timestep in all three generations (n_nonzero = 0/2529, 0/6229, 0/2657); charged_trna_conc[ARG] = 0 throughout; effectiveElongationRate = 0.0 at every timestep. The fourth fails, and with it the headline. Free arginine (GrowthLimits/aa_conc[ARG], uM) rises 288 -> 1498 within generation 0 (WT ~215 uM), then FALLS 1497 -> 1272 in generation 1 and collapses 1272 -> 251 in generation 2; generation means 1436, 1441, 772 uM. So the pool accumulates only at gen 0 and is 46% lower by gen 2. The uncharged cognate tRNA pool — the actual RelA stimulus — also differs strongly by depth: 29.09, 43.33, 12.34 uM (gen 1 is +49% over gen 0, gen 2 is -58%); the same pattern holds in all four seeds and all four genes (e.g. pheS s0: 5.85, 7.65, 1.58). Total charged tRNA summed over all 21 families is not zero either (262.9, 399.7, 115.6 uM) — only the cognate family is zero. The generation-2 divergence coincides with the QC flag (growth mean 0.0012 vs 0.00023 in WT, flagged implausible_channel).
suggested_fix: Restrict the identity claim to what is actually identical: 'the synthetase, the cognate charged-tRNA pool and the elongation rate are identically zero at every timestep of every generation.' Drop 'the free amino acid accumulates unconsumed' as a depth-invariant statement — it holds at generation 0 only; by generation 2 free arginine has fallen to 251 uM. And note that the uncharged cognate tRNA pool itself varies ~3.5-fold across the three depths, so the stimulus is not constant.

claim: Only the remaining RelA differs between generations, halved at each division.
evidence: Both halves fail. (1) 'Only RelA differs': as measured above, uncharged cognate tRNA changes by ~3.5-fold across depths (argS s0: 29.09 / 43.33 / 12.34 uM), free cognate amino acid by ~1.9-fold (1436 / 1441 / 772 uM), and total charged tRNA by ~3.5-fold (263 / 400 / 116 uM). (2) 'Halved at each division': on GrowthLimits/rela_conc, the gen0->gen1 ratio is roughly halving (0.317–0.560 across the 16 KO seed-runs, mean ~0.44) but the gen1->gen2 ratio is 0.033–0.139 (mean ~0.084) — a 7x to 30x drop, an order of magnitude away from 0.5, i.e. log2 slope ~-3.6 rather than the -1 that src/cellarium/dilution.py registers as PREDICTED_SLOPE for pure halving. On RelA monomer counts (MonomerCounts/monomerCounts, RELA-MONOMER[c]) the decay is steeper than halving but more regular: argS s0 79.4 / 32.3 / 13.2, ratios 0.41 and 0.41; across argS and pheS all eight seeds the per-division ratios run 0.24–0.44 (mean ~0.33), i.e. roughly a three-fold loss per division, not a two-fold one.
suggested_fix: Replace with the measured behaviour and name the observable. E.g. 'RelA falls faster than pure dilution: monomer counts drop ~3-fold per division (ratios 0.24–0.44 over 8 seed-runs) rather than 2-fold, and RelA concentration drops 0.44x then 0.08x per division.' Delete 'only' — uncharged tRNA, free amino acid and total charged tRNA all vary substantially with depth as well.

claim: The simulator represents the mechanism: ppGpp synthesis runs proportional to RelA concentration times an active fraction that saturates with the number of ribosomes carrying an uncharged tRNA.
evidence: Confirmed in the source actually used by these runs. models/ecoli/processes/polypeptide_elongation.py, ppgpp_metabolite_changes(): `ribosomes_bound_to_uncharged = ribosome_conc_a_site * saturated_uncharged`; `competitive_inhibition = 1 + ribosomes_bound_to_uncharged / ppgpp_params['KD_RelA']`; `frac_rela = 1 / (KD_RelA / ribosomes_bound_to_uncharged * inhibition_product / competitive_inhibition + 1)`; `v_rela_syn = ppgpp_params['k_RelA'] * rela_conc * frac_rela`. That is exactly first-order in rela_conc times a fraction that saturates in ribosomes_bound_to_uncharged (in the single-species limit frac_rela reduces to R_u/(KD_RelA + R_u)). The same four lines are byte-identical in the overlay shipped with this repo, model_overlay/files/models/ecoli/processes/polypeptide_elongation.py lines 1444, 1454, 1457, 1460, so the description applies to the code that produced runs_seed_aars. Two refinements the sentence elides: the saturation is per-amino-acid across 21 species with a cross-species competitive-inhibition product (`inhibition_product = np.prod(competitive_inhibition)`), so one family's uncharged-bound ribosomes suppress the others' contribution; and total synthesis is v_rela_syn.sum() + k_SpoT_syn*spot_conc, set against a SpoT degradation term v_deg that is itself inhibited by uncharged tRNA — so net ppGpp is not RelA synthesis alone.

claim: At generation 0 the uncharged tRNA pool stands at 4.7 times wild type while the active fraction falls to 0.55 of wild type.
evidence: Both numbers reproduce for argS. Computing over generation 0, 4 seeds, gene_knockout_000644 vs depth-matched wildtype_704585: total uncharged tRNA (GrowthLimits/uncharged_trna_conc summed over the 21 families, time-mean) gives KO/WT = 4.658 -> 4.7, tight across seeds (per-seed ratios 4.95, 5.00, 4.53, 4.23). The RelA active fraction, recovered from the rate law as sum(GrowthLimits/rela_syn) / rela_conc (= k_RelA * sum(frac_rela), so k_RelA cancels in the ratio), gives KO/WT = 0.549 -> 0.55. Two caveats. First, the active-fraction ratio is far less stable than the pool ratio: per-seed values are 0.378, 0.577, 0.725, 0.707 (the 0.55 is the ratio of means; the mean of per-seed ratios is 0.60). Second, neither number generalises to the other three designs — alaS 2.60x / 1.00x, gltX 2.53x / 0.56x, pheS 1.03x / 0.34x — so if the sentence is read as a property of the four-knockout panel rather than of argS it is not supported.
suggested_fix: If the sentence is meant panel-wide, restate as argS-specific ('in the argS knockout the total uncharged tRNA pool stands at 4.7x wild type while the RelA active fraction falls to 0.55x'), and either give the other three designs (alaS 2.6x/1.00x, gltX 2.5x/0.56x, pheS 1.0x/0.34x) or say the pattern is heterogeneous. Consider reporting the active-fraction ratio with its seed spread (0.38–0.73, n=4), which is wide enough that 0.55 alone overstates the precision.

Executed `capability.check('operon_specific_rrna_knockout')` -> {can_answer: false, report_a_number: false, why_not: 'no_elongation_model_represents_it', refusal: 'The model as configured CANNOT represent operon_specific_rrna_knockout…'} with no numeric field. claim: Cellwright can only propose new runs to a human approval gate, which is the sole path back to the simulator.
evidence: <repo>\src\cellarium\launch.py:85 `propose()` vets and appends a request with status 'pending_approval'/'blocked' to the queue at data/launch_queue.json (QUEUE resolved absolutely, launch.py:24); launch.py:289 `approve_and_run()` is the only function that calls manifest.campaign (line 319). claim: Ribosome occupancy rather than the uncharged pool is the trigger, because a ribosome carries uncharged tRNA only while elongating — so removing the synthetase outright halts translation before any ribosome stalls and the sensor never sees its trigger state.
evidence: SOURCE (C:/dev/wcEcoli/models/ecoli/processes/polypeptide_elongation.py): the occupancy term is NOT gated on active elongation. `ribosome_conc` is the TOTAL active-ribosome count (line 1095/1108 request path, line 1320 evolve path: `self.counts_to_molar * self.process.active_ribosomes.total_count()`), not the elongating subset. The zero-elongation case is explicitly handled so occupancy stays NONZERO: line 1519-1520 `if v_rib == 0: ribosome_conc_a_site = f * ribosome_conc`, and line 1331-1334 carries the comment 'Need to include the next amino acid the ribosome sees for certain cases where elongation does not occur, otherwise f will be NaN' with `aa_at_ribosome = aas_used + next_amino_acid_count`. Decisively, when charged tRNA is EXACTLY zero (the aaRS-KO case), `saturated_charged`=0 makes `a_site_weights` non-finite and the mask at lines 1552-1554 sets `ribosomes_bound_to_uncharged = ribosome_conc * f`, i.e. the FULL A-site share — the sensor is pinned at MAXIMUM, not zero. TRACES (no listener column is literally named 'occupancy'; the only downstream observable is GrowthLimits/rela_syn = k_RelA*[RelA]*frac_rela, which is monotone in ribosomes_bound_to_uncharged): argS KO vs WT, generation 0, 4 seeds each (runs_seed_aars/cellarium/gene_knockout_000644 vs .../wildtype_704585) — uncharged pool 29.615 vs 6.357 uM = 4.66x (this DOES reproduce the '4.7x'); charged ARG exactly 0.00 in the KO; rela_syn for ARG 0.1449 (KO) vs 0.00045 (WT) = ~320x UP, and in the KO ARG carries 100% of total RelA synthesis (argmax = ARG[c], rela_max_aa == rela_tot on all 4 seeds); activeRibosomeAllocated 18,290 (KO) vs 20,659 (WT) = 89% of WT. Total rela_syn is 0.1449 vs 0.2312 (63% of WT) — lower, but nowhere near ~0. ppGpp is 44.8 vs 61.1 uM. The KO's lower TOTAL RelA output is explained by the rate law's np.prod competitive-inhibition term (lines 1557-1563), which caps total synthesis at k_RelA*[RelA] once one arm saturates and drives the other 20 arms toward zero — not by the sensor failing to see its trigger.
suggested_fix: Drop the 'never sees its trigger state' mechanism. The traces show the opposite: at 4.7x uncharged pool the argS-KO ARG RelA arm is saturated (rela_syn ~320x WT, carrying 100% of RelA synthesis) with ribosomes at 89% of WT. The correct statement is that RelA's competitive-inhibition product caps total ppGpp synthesis at one saturated arm's worth, so concentrating all occupancy on a single amino acid yields LESS total synthesis than WT's many partially-occupied arms — a property of the rate law, not of translation halting. Also correct 'computed from actively elongating ribosomes': the code uses total active ribosomes and explicitly keeps f defined when elongation is zero (line 1331-1334).
